rationale: The recorded premise that the replay's batch count follows the number of replayed log entries is imprecise, and a construction run of the boundary harness exposed it: a replay ending at index 2049 returned while one ending at 2050 did not, although the entry-based formula gives 129 batches for both. The batch count follows the entries that processLogs turns into commit tuples, so this batch corrects that behaviour and submits the fixed experiment that places the boundary exactly at the channel's capacity.

knowledge.changed_premise: The earlier statement said processLogs batches committed entries; the batch count is set by the entries that prepareLog turns into commit tuples, not by every replayed entry. No-op entries consume no batch slot, and configuration entries do so only above protocol version 2, so any batch count computed from a log index range is an upper bound.
knowledge.statement: processLogs walks the committed range from lastApplied+1 to the given index, appends a commit tuple only for entries prepareLog accepts (LogCommand and LogBarrier always, LogConfiguration when protocolVersion > 2; LogNoop and the deprecated peer entries produce none), flushes a batch whenever the batch reaches config.MaxAppendEntries, and delivers each batch with a select whose only cases are a send on r.fsmMutateCh and a receive on r.shutdownCh; when the channel has no free slot and the node is not shutting down, the send waits indefinitely.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to every caller of processLogs: the startup replay in restoreFromCommittedLogs, the leader commit path and the follower AppendEntries path (raft.go:1296-1364 with prepareLog at raft.go:1364-1391).

scope.description: Two single-voter prefixes at Config.MaxAppendEntries 16 with no snapshot, built so that their persisted commit index ends at 2049 and 2050. Each prefix is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft is called in a goroutine, and the harness waits up to 8000ms. Both events report the entries in the replayed range and, separately, the number of entries in that range that become commit tuples and the batches those tuples need.
assumptions: The prefix applies commands one at a time and stops as soon as the store's commit index reaches the target, and the harness reports the value it actually reached.
The tuple count is derived by scanning the replayed range for LogCommand, LogBarrier and LogConfiguration entries, which is what prepareLog accepts at the default protocol version 3.
No snapshot exists on either prefix, so the replay starts at index 1 and the whole range is delivered.
The block is judged by non-return within 8000ms plus a stack sample naming the replay frames; permanence comes from the source, since the channel's only consumer starts after the replay returns.
excluded: No production store, no multi-node group and no default SnapshotThreshold: the point of this case is the boundary in batches, not the reachability of the range under default settings.
Only two points are placed, one batch below and one batch above the capacity, so no finer scan of the edge is attempted.

experiment.prefix: For each target the harness creates an in-memory transport and a commit-tracking log store, configures inmemConfig with RestoreCommittedLogs true, MaxAppendEntries 16, SnapshotThreshold 1<<30 and SnapshotInterval one hour, calls BootstrapCluster with the single voter and NewRaft with a fresh MockFSM, waits for real leadership, and then applies one command at a time, re-reading the store's commit index after each apply, until it reaches the target. It records the commands applied, the log's last index, the staged commit index, the number of tuples in the replayed range, the batches those tuples need and the entry-based count, then shuts the prefix down. The restart creates a new transport on the same address, copies the config with RestoreCommittedLogs true, and calls NewRaft in a separate goroutine on the same stores with a fresh MockFSM; the main goroutine waits up to 8000ms and, on non-return, samples all goroutine stacks and reports the excerpt around the first frame naming restoreFromCommittedLogs.
experiment.responsibility: NewRaft owns completion of its own startup work; the size of the replay it performs is set by the entries that become commit tuples, so the caller cannot infer the reachable replay from the log's index range alone.

comparisons.description: A replay of exactly 128 delivered batches fills the channel without exceeding it, so NewRaft must return.

A replay of 129 delivered batches needs one more batch than the channel holds, so NewRaft must still return; the pair with the 128-batch case places the bound at the channel's capacity in delivered batches rather than at a count of replayed log entries.
